record.question: What is a Telegram trading bot and why does it beat manual trading?
record.answer: A Telegram trading bot is an automated tool that executes crypto trades directly from a Telegram chat interface. It beats manual trading because it removes human latency entirely. Memecoin launches and prediction market opportunities appear and disappear in seconds — a bot monitors contracts, tracks wallets, and executes orders faster than any human can. The four main categories are: sniper bots (buy tokens immediately after liquidity appears), copy trading bots (automatically mirror profitable wallets), prediction market bots (replicate trades from top forecasters), and multi-chain bots (operate across multiple blockchains simultaneously). Not using a bot means voluntarily surrendering alpha to those who do.

record.question: Why is Solana the best chain for memecoin sniping?
record.answer: Solana dominates memecoin sniping because its infrastructure is optimized for speed and minimal cost. Block times of ~400ms, transaction fees under $0.01, and up to 65,000 TPS make high-frequency bot trading economically viable. Crucially, Solana has no global mempool — success depends on same-block participation rather than gas bidding wars. Pump.fun allows anyone to launch tokens instantly; liquidity migrates to Raydium; Jupiter routes trades through the most efficient pools. This creates thousands of daily launch opportunities that bots like Trojan can capture in under 2 seconds. The combination of speed, low cost, and a thriving memecoin culture (Pump.fun, Moonshot, LetsBonk.fun) makes Solana the optimal chain.

The migration moment is when many traders try to buy simultaneously, making speed critical. Trojan's Migration Sniper fires automatically the instant migration occurs — no manual monitoring needed. It also auto-exits if a migration fails. This is one of Trojan's most unique features not universally available in competing bots.

record.question: How does crypto copy trading work with Telegram bots?
record.answer: Copy trading bots monitor a target wallet's on-chain transactions in real time. The moment the target wallet executes a buy or sell, the bot mirrors that exact action — same token, proportional or configured size — within milliseconds. This exploits information asymmetry: skilled traders often have superior research, insider knowledge, or analytical models. Manual copy trading is structurally impossible at competitive speed. The key parameters to configure: which wallets to copy, how much to allocate per trade, minimum liquidity threshold, maximum market cap, stop-loss triggers per position, and whether to auto-sell when the copied wallet sells. record.question: How do I pick the right wallets to copy trade?

(3) Check win rate AND average gain — a 70% win rate with small gains may underperform a 50% win rate with large gains. (4) Analyze drawdown — peak-to-trough loss tells you the worst-case scenario you should expect. (5) Diversify across 3–5 wallets rather than concentrating on one. (6) Rotate weekly — reassess each wallet's recent performance and replace consistently underperforming ones. For Polymarket, prioritize wallets specializing in a specific category (elections, macro, sports) rather than generalists.

Bots are essential because: (1) prices move instantly when new information emerges — manual entry misses the entry price by 10–20%; (2) skilled traders (smart money) open positions before the market reacts; (3) copy trading these skilled traders requires millisecond execution the moment their position is taken.
